title: CloudFront with S3 — Origin Access Control (OAC) and legacy OAI
hook: Your static site bucket should stay private. Origin Access Control (OAC) lets CloudFront fetch objects with SigV4-signed requests while the rest of the internet gets AccessDenied.

blocks.text: Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) is the most common CloudFront origin for static sites, SPAs, and downloadable assets. Origin Access Control (OAC) is the current mechanism: CloudFront assumes an IAM service principal and signs GetObject (and optionally PutObject) requests to a private bucket. Origin Access Identity (OAI) is the legacy model using a special CloudFront user in bucket policy — still supported but AWS recommends OAC for new work because it supports all S3 regions, SSE-KMS, and dynamic HTTP methods.

entries.plainDefinition: CloudFront feature that signs S3 requests so only your distribution can read private objects.
entries.example: Bucket policy allows s3:GetObject for cloudfront.amazonaws.com with SourceArn condition.

entries.plainDefinition: Legacy CloudFront IAM principal embedded in S3 bucket policy.
entries.example: Canonical user ID in bucket policy — migrate to OAC.

entries.plainDefinition: Account and bucket-level guardrails preventing public ACLs and policies.
entries.example: Keep all four Block Public Access settings ON for static site buckets.

entries.plainDefinition: bucket.s3.region.amazonaws.com — required origin domain for OAC, not the website endpoint.

blocks.text: Public S3 buckets caused thousands of data leaks. The correct pattern: Block Public Access ON, no public ACL, bucket policy grants GetObject only to your CloudFront distribution ARN. Users never talk to S3 directly — only CloudFront URLs. OAC also enables SSE-KMS encrypted objects without making keys public. Interviews test whether you know the bucket policy Principal and Condition format, not just 'make bucket private.'

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: REST endpoint + OAC + bucket policy with Service principal cloudfront.amazonaws.com and AWS:SourceArn = distribution ARN. Block all public access. Do not use S3 website endpoint with OAC.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — OAC, distribution, and bucket policy
snippet.code:
Resources:
  StaticOAC:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::OriginAccessControl
    Properties:
      OriginAccessControlConfig:
        Name: app-static-oac
        OriginAccessControlOriginType: s3
        SigningBehavior: always
        SigningProtocol: sigv4

  StaticBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: app-static-prod-123456789012
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true

  StaticDistribution:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::Distribution
    Properties:
      DistributionConfig:
        Enabled: true
        Origins:
          - Id: S3Origin
            DomainName: !GetAtt StaticBucket.RegionalDomainName
            OriginAccessControlId: !GetAtt StaticOAC.Id
            S3OriginConfig:
              OriginAccessIdentity: ''
        DefaultCacheBehavior:
          TargetOriginId: S3Origin
          ViewerProtocolPolicy: redirect-to-https
          CachePolicyId: 658327ea-f89d-4fab-a63d-7e88639e58f6

  StaticBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref StaticBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowCloudFrontServicePrincipal
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: cloudfront.amazonaws.com
            Action: s3:GetObject
            Resource: !Sub '${StaticBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                AWS:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:aws:cloudfront::${AWS::AccountId}:distribution/${StaticDistribution}'
snippet.explanation: OAC resource links to S3 origin. Bucket policy grants GetObject only when request comes from that specific distribution ARN. Empty OriginAccessIdentity retires OAI on new origins.

snippet.label: CLI — verify bucket is not public and test direct access
snippet.code:
aws s3api get-public-access-block --bucket app-static-prod-123456789012

# Should return AccessDenied (good)
aws s3api get-object \
  --bucket app-static-prod-123456789012 \
  --key index.html /tmp/index.html

# CloudFront URL should work
curl -sI https://app.example.com/index.html | head -5
snippet.explanation: Direct S3 API call without CloudFront credentials fails. Only CloudFront OAC-signed requests succeed.

snippet.label: CLI — sync build output to S3 with correct cache headers
snippet.code:
aws s3 sync ./dist/browser s3://app-static-prod-123456789012/ \
  --delete \
  --cache-control 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable' \
  --exclude 'index.html' \
  --exclude '*.html'

aws s3 cp ./dist/browser/index.html s3://app-static-prod-123456789012/index.html \
  --cache-control 'no-cache, must-revalidate' \
  --content-type 'text/html'
snippet.explanation: Deploy hashed assets with long TTL. index.html short TTL so CloudFront fetches new script references after sync without invalidation.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — SSE-KMS bucket with OAC
snippet.code:
StaticBucket:
  Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
  Properties:
    BucketEncryption:
      ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
        - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
            SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
            KMSMasterKeyID: !GetAtt AppKey.Arn
# OAC supports KMS — ensure KMS key policy allows CloudFront via S3
# OAI did not support KMS the same way; common migration driver
snippet.explanation: OAC + KMS is a senior talking point. Key policy must allow S3 to decrypt; CloudFront accesses via S3's KMS integration.

blocks.title: S3 + CloudFront vs public static hosting
Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Using S3 static website endpoint (s3-website-) as origin with OAC — use REST regional domain. Forgetting AWS:SourceArn condition — any distribution in the account could read. Leaving Block Public Access off 'temporarily.' Mixing OAI and OAC on the same origin without policy update.

blocks.text: OAI migration: create OAC, attach to origin, add new bucket policy statement, deploy, verify CloudFront, remove OAI statement, delete OAI. Cross-account S3 origin requires bucket policy in asset account and distribution in CDN account with correct SourceArn. How to prove it in production: attempt direct https://bucket.s3.region.amazonaws.com/key — must 403; CloudWatch S3 4xx should not spike from internet scanners if policy is tight. Use S3 server access logging only if needed — CloudFront access logs are usually enough.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'make the bucket public read-only for CloudFront.' Strong answer: OAC with Service principal, SourceArn condition, Block Public Access on, REST endpoint origin.

interviewTakeaways: OAC signs SigV4 GetObject to private S3; bucket policy allows cloudfront.amazonaws.com with AWS:SourceArn = distribution ARN.
Use S3 regional REST domain as origin, not the website endpoint; keep Block Public Access enabled.
Deploy with content-hashed assets (long Cache-Control) and short TTL on index.html — sync via aws s3 sync in CI.
60s: Private bucket, OAC on distribution, bucket policy SourceArn, users only hit CloudFront. OAI is legacy.
Follow-up: how does OAC differ for SSE-KMS objects versus SSE-S3?
commonPitfalls: Public bucket for static hosting — rejection answer due to data leak history and missing defense in depth.
Strong answer: OAC + private bucket + SourceArn condition + no website endpoint.
Bucket policy missing SourceArn — any CloudFront distribution in account could read.
403 on all paths because OriginAccessControlId not attached to origin.
